title: Probabilistic Slew Scheduler for architecture & sequence-length aware kernel selection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a runtime "probabilistic slew scheduler" that blends architecture fingerprints and sequence-length conditioned priors to pick among multiple attention/kernel implementations (fused attention, chunked-attn, quantized matmul kernels, etc.). Goal is lower median and p95 latency for mixed workloads while limiting kernel-switch churn and preserving deterministic fallbacks for SLO-critical traffic.

design_notes: Core idea: compute a posterior score per kernel K = log_prior(arch, seqlen, phase) + log_likelihood(observed_latency_history_K) then sample top-K with a temperature that decays with confidence. Use slew-rate limiter (time-windowed exponential moving average) to prevent hasty switches.

Architecture fingerprinting: lightweight descriptor based on GPU compute capability, SM count, memory bandwidth class and observed macro-bench markers; fingerprint strings must be stable across minor driver updates.

Seqlen bucketing: coarse buckets [<=16, 17-64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024] derived from production token distribution. Per-bucket priors are learned from historical telemetry and warmed from microbench results.

Attention impls: treat fused attention, block-sparse shim, and quantized matmul path as separate kernel variants with different tail behaviors. Penalize kernels with higher variance unless tail wins justify risk.
Safety: always expose 'conservative' kernel selection flag. For SLO-sensitive customers, skip exploration and use fixed kernel mapping configured via account metadata.
Operational: metrics emitted - kernel_choice, kernel_switch_count, decision_confidence, candidate_scores, slew_window_ms, fallback_trigger_reason.
Trade-offs: exploration improves long-run cost/latency but can worsen tail for short bursts. Slew-window reduces exploration speed and therefore the adaptation speed to sudden workload shifts.
Rollout plan includes a short canary then staged ramp with automated rollback on a small set of telemetry gates.
Decision: adopt probabilistic sampling with conservative default temperature and a 500ms default slew-window configurable per deployment tier.

Open question: should we include sequence-phase (prefill vs decode) as a separate conditioning factor for priors? Initial experiments show different winners; plan to add phase conditioning in follow-up sprint if canary is safe.
Docs: design doc in Confluence and compatibility matrix to map kernels to model families (e.g., LLaMA-like, Mistral-like).
test_plan: Unit tests for prior/posterior scoring and deterministic seed path.
Integration tests with runtime simulator across A100/T4/V100 profiles.
Canary: 10% traffic for 72 hours with alerts on latency_p95, error_rate, kernel_switchs_per_min.
Chaos test: inject synthetic seqlen distribution shifts and ensure slew avoids oscillation.
Backfill: ability to replay decisions via deterministic seed for debugging.
Performance acceptance: p50 <= baseline*0.95 or p95 <= baseline*0.98 on mixed workloads, no increase in error-rate > 0.1%.
Cost acceptance: cost-per-token should not increase by more than 3% for canary cohort.
Documentation: ops runbook and feature flagging instructions completed before release.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2321 must be merged and feature-flag default OFF for existing customers.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge behind feature flag, internal QA only.
Stage 1: Canary 10% of internal traffic (non-customer) for 48-72 hours, monitor gates.
Stage 2: Canary on opt-in customers (low SLO sensitivity) for 1 week; collect seqlen-phase breakdowns.
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 25% and then 50% with per-region toggles; keep conservative defaults for Dedicated tiers.
Rollback criteria: p95 regression > 8% for 10m rolling window OR error-rate > 0.1% OR kernel_switch_rate spikes > 3x baseline.
Post-mortem: any rollback triggers immediate incident review and a decision whether to disable exploration globally.
